name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
memory_bandwidth_basis: GDDR6X 21 Gbps data rate x 384-bit / 8 = 1008 GB/s (NVIDIA Ada whitepaper Appendix A: 'Memory Clock (Data Rate) 21 Gbps', 'Memory Bandwidth 1008 GB/sec')
notes: AUDIT 2026-10-03 (NVIDIA dense/sparse convention re-verified from the primary Ada whitepaper PDF, no values changed): NVIDIA's Ada GPU architecture whitepaper prints its consumer spec tables in the same 'DENSE/SPARSE' form with the footnote 'Effective TOPS / TFLOPS using the Sparsity Feature'. AD102 appendix: 'Peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP16 Accumulate 330.3/660.6', 'Peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate 165.2/330.4', 'Peak BF16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate 165.2/330.4', 'Peak TF32 Tensor TFLOPS 82.6/165.2', 'Peak INT8 Tensor TOPS 660.6/1321.2', 'Peak INT4 Tensor TOPS 1321.2/2642.4'. So the five dense:false rows on this record - bf16 330.4, tf32 165.2, fp8 660.6, int8 1321.2, int4 2642.4 - are each the SPARSE column of the printed pair, with the dense twin stored separately. Correct. The fp8 660.6 row is the paper's 'FP16 with FP16 accumulate' rate; Ada has no native FP8 accumulate path, which is why this figure equals the FP16-accumulate FP16 number rather than half of it.
